title: Example Figures — Realistic, Never Toy or Placeholder
description: Figures inside an example must be values a practitioner would recognise, at the right magnitude and shape for the domain: hex base and bound addresses, power-of-two page and frame sizes, real port and RFC numbers, plausible PIDs, byte counts, ms timings, standard field widths. A toy number teaches a toy mental model — 'base = 5' is not an address. Round numbers are fine as COUNTS of things (3 processes, 4 frames) but never as an address, a size or an identifier, and a placeholder ('some address', 'value X', 'xyz') is never acceptable. Deterministic half: a working_example slide carries at least 2 concrete values and no banned placeholder. LLM half: are those values plausible for the domain?
criterion: Every example uses domain-plausible figures with correct magnitude and format; at least two concrete values per worked example; no placeholders anywhere in the doc.

rubric.5: Every figure is one a practitioner would recognise, correctly formatted for its kind.
rubric.3: Figures are concrete but one is implausible or oddly formatted (a decimal where hex is conventional, an off-by-magnitude size).
rubric.1: Toy values used as addresses/sizes/identifiers, a placeholder, or an 'example' with no concrete values at all.

input.example: Process 4312 has base register 0x00400000 and a 12 KB limit; a 4 KB page maps to frame 0x0000C, giving physical 0x0000C2B4.

cases.rationale: Hex addresses, power-of-two page size, plausible PID.

input.example: 3 processes compete for 4 identical tape drives; P1 holds 2, requests 1 more.

cases.rationale: Small round numbers used as COUNTS of things — correct here.

input.example: The base register holds 5 and the offset is 3, so the physical address is 8.

cases.rationale: Toy numbers as addresses. A learner leaves with the impression addresses are single digits.

input.example: Add the offset to some address in the base register to get the physical address.

cases.rationale: Placeholder instead of a figure, and nothing is actually worked through.

input.example: A page of size 1000 bytes is mapped to frame number X.

cases.rationale: Page sizes are powers of two (4 KB, 8 KB), and 'frame number X' is a placeholder.
